member.name: T:Kdouja.Abstractions.CommonOptions.EngineOptions
member.summary: Configuration options specifying operational behavior, resource limits, and performance tuning parameters for the KdoujaKV storage engine.

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: These options govern critical aspects of the storage engine lifecycle, including write path buffering (MemTable limits, WAL segments, write backpressure), read path optimizations (block cache capacity, compression, and Direct I/O configurations), and background database operations (compaction thresholds and bandwidth rate-limiting). Adjusting these values directly affects LSM-tree write amplification, read latency, memory footprint, and disk wear.

Performance Implications: Over-allocating the block cache or MemTable threshold can trigger Out Of Memory (OOM) scenarios under heavy write pressure, while under-allocating may trigger excessive write amplification and disk I/O due to premature flushing. Enabling Direct I/O eliminates double-buffering by avoiding the operating system's page cache but requires strict alignment constraints on buffer allocations.

member.name: P:Kdouja.Abstractions.CommonOptions.EngineOptions.BaseDirectory
member.summary: Gets or sets the absolute or relative file system directory path where all storage engine state is persisted.

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: Contains the write-ahead logs (WAL), active SSTables, manifests, lock files, and temporary compaction files. It is crucial that the execution context has exclusive read, write, delete, and directory manipulation permissions in this location.
Concurrency: Multiple database engine instances should never share the same base directory concurrently; doing so will result in manifest corruption, WAL conflicts, and data loss.

member.name: P:Kdouja.Abstractions.CommonOptions.EngineOptions.MemTableFlushThresholdBytes
member.summary: Gets or sets the threshold in bytes that determines when the current active in-memory MemTable is frozen and scheduled to be flushed as an L0 SSTable.

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: Regulates the balance between memory utilization and write throughput. Once the MemTable reaches this byte limit, it transitions to a read-only state, and a background thread serializes its content to an L0 SSTable on non-volatile storage.

Performance Implications: A larger threshold increases write throughput by reducing the number of small SSTables, which also mitigates write/read amplification. However, it raises memory overhead and recovery time during crash restarts as the WAL must replay more operations to rebuild the unsaved MemTable state.

member.name: P:Kdouja.Abstractions.CommonOptions.EngineOptions.MaxL0FilesBeforeCompaction
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum count of Level 0 (L0) SSTable files allowed to accumulate before triggering an L0-to-L1 compaction run.

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: L0 SSTables contain overlapping key ranges. Therefore, read lookups must scan all L0 files if they cannot be discarded by Bloom filters. Compaction merges overlapping L0 SSTables and writes sorted, non-overlapping L1 SSTables.

Performance Implications: Setting this value too low causes aggressive compaction, leading to high write amplification and I/O starvation. Conversely, setting it too high causes read lookups to scan too many files, increasing read amplification and query latency.

member.name: P:Kdouja.Abstractions.CommonOptions.EngineOptions.Compression
member.summary: Gets or sets the compression codec utilized to compress data blocks within generated SSTables on disk.

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: Compressed blocks minimize disk usage and reduce I/O transfer volume. However, decompression introduces CPU overhead on the read hot-path.

Performance Implications: is recommended for high-throughput scenarios to achieve rapid decompression speeds. For cold data or archival storage, stronger compression codecs (like ZSTD/Deflate) can be utilized at the cost of additional CPU utilization.

member.name: P:Kdouja.Abstractions.CommonOptions.EngineOptions.EnableDirectIO
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether Direct I/O (O_DIRECT / FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING) is enabled for reading and writing data blocks in the page store.

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: Bypasses the operating system's kernel page cache. This eliminates double-buffering (where pages reside in both the OS cache and the engine's internal block cache), providing predictable latencies and preventing CPU-cache thrashing.

Performance Implications: Must be enabled in production environments targeting low-latency SSDs. Note that when Direct I/O is enabled, all buffer pointers, sizes, and file offsets must be aligned to the hardware sector size boundaries (typically 4096 bytes).

member.name: P:Kdouja.Abstractions.CommonOptions.EngineOptions.PageSizeBytes
member.summary: Gets or sets the fixed page size, in bytes, allocated by the underlying page store block device manager.

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: Defines the fundamental unit of transfer between the storage engine's memory pool and physical storage. This value must align with the physical sector or page size of the underlying storage hardware.

Performance Implications: Typically set to 4096 bytes (4KB) to match standard SSD page sizes. Incorrect alignment or non-multiple page sizes will trigger alignment faults, especially when is configured to true.

member.name: P:Kdouja.Abstractions.CommonOptions.EngineOptions.EnableWalFsync
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the storage engine forces a physical disk synchronization (fsync/flush) on the Write-Ahead Log (WAL) for every append transaction.

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: Guarantees transaction durability (ACID properties). If configured to true, a transaction is not acknowledged as committed until the WAL records have been physically written to non-volatile storage media.

Performance Implications: Setting this to true provides maximum durability but restricts write throughput to the physical disk's synchronization frequency (IOPS). Setting it to false allows the operating system to buffer WAL writes, dramatically increasing performance at the risk of losing recent commits in the event of OS crashes or power failures.

member.name: P:Kdouja.Abstractions.CommonOptions.EngineOptions.BlockCacheCapacity
member.summary: Gets or sets the capacity of the block cache, representing the maximum number of decompressed data blocks retained in memory.

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: Speeds up read paths by caching decompressed SSTable blocks, bypassing block decompression and storage device I/O.

Performance Implications: Direct trade-off between heap allocation and performance. If too small, cache miss ratios increase, leading to high CPU consumption from decompression and disk read latencies. If too large, it may cause high GC pressure or lead to out-of-memory errors.

member.name: P:Kdouja.Abstractions.CommonOptions.EngineOptions.WalSegmentSizeBytes
member.summary: Gets or sets the threshold size, in bytes, before the active Write-Ahead Log (WAL) file segment is rotated and closed.

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: Restricts the maximum size of individual WAL files on disk. As old MemTables are flushed to disk as SSTables, the associated WAL segments containing operations belonging to those MemTables are garbage collected.
Performance Implications: Smaller segment sizes prevent storage waste and simplify file cleanup operations but may trigger frequent file handles creation and metadata updates on the filesystem.

member.name: P:Kdouja.Abstractions.CommonOptions.EngineOptions.WalEncryptionKey

member.name: P:Kdouja.Abstractions.CommonOptions.EngineOptions.MaxL0FilesBackpressureThreshold
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum count of Level 0 (L0) SSTables that triggers write stalling or write backpressure.

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: Acts as a protective circuit breaker. If the rate of incoming writes exceeds the background compaction speed, L0 files accumulate. When this threshold is crossed, the engine artificially slows down incoming writes to allow compaction to catch up.
Performance Implications: Prevents infinite read degradation and memory exhaust errors, guaranteeing system stability under sustained peak write stress at the expense of temporary throughput drops.

member.name: P:Kdouja.Abstractions.CommonOptions.EngineOptions.BaseLevelTargetSizeBytes
member.summary: Gets or sets the target size, in bytes, for Level 1 (L1) of the LSM-tree.

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: Establishes the baseline size limit for compaction levels. Each subsequent level's capacity limit is computed using this base level size and the .
Performance Implications: Modifying the level target sizes changes the frequency of compaction events at L1, affecting both write amplification and disk I/O.

member.name: P:Kdouja.Abstractions.CommonOptions.EngineOptions.LevelSizeMultiplier
member.summary: Gets or sets the exponential growth multiplier factor for computing size limits of consecutive LSM-tree compaction levels.

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: If Level 1 target size is L and the multiplier is T, Level 2 size limit is L * T, Level 3 is L * T^2, and so on.

Performance Implications: A higher multiplier decreases the total number of levels (lowering read amplification), but increases the amount of data rewritten during each individual compaction step (increasing write amplification and write latency spikes). A value of 10 is standard.

member.name: P:Kdouja.Abstractions.CommonOptions.EngineOptions.CompactionBandwidthRateBytesPerSecond
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum cumulative disk read/write bandwidth in bytes per second allocated to background compaction threads.

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: Background compactions are extremely I/O-intensive. If unrestricted, compaction can saturate disk bandwidth, causing latency spikes on the critical read/write path of client operations.

Performance Implications: Configuring a limit (e.g. 50 MB/s) isolates and guarantees disk I/O capacity for active client queries. Setting this value to 0 or a negative integer disables rate limiting, allowing compactions to execute at maximum hardware capability.

member.name: T:Kdouja.Abstractions.CommonOptions.KeyPrefix
member.summary: Specifies byte-level prefix identifiers used for logical namespacing and keyspace partitioning within the LSM-tree key-value database.

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: In a log-structured merge-tree (LSM-tree), all data resides in a single sorted keyspace. Prefixing keys with a single byte partitions the keyspace into distinct namespaces (e.g., file metadata, file indices, node status, and encryption keys). This enables fast range queries, prefix-seeking iterators, and logical isolation of engine subsystem metadata without the overhead of maintaining separate physical databases.

Performance Implications: Placing the prefix byte as the first byte of keys allows binary key comparisons (lexicographical comparison on ) to immediately branch or terminate. This prevents deep scanning of subsequent payload bytes during seek operations and optimizes SSTable index lookups.

member.name: T:Kdouja.Abstractions.CommonOptions.ReadOptions
member.summary: Configures the behavior, consistency requirements, and isolation level of read operations within the storage engine.

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: Regulates whether a read operation operates on a live, mutable view of the database or binds to a static, point-in-time logical snapshot. In MVCC-based (Multi-Version Concurrency Control) systems, read options dictate version visibility ranges.

Performance Implications: Using a snapshot () ensures stable, repeatable reads during long-running range queries. remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: Represents a logical sequence number barrier. Any data updates with a sequence number larger than this snapshot's sequence number will be filtered out during query execution.
Concurrency: The engine ensures that snapshots are immutable and thread-safe. A single snapshot can be concurrently read by multiple threads.

member.name: T:Kdouja.Abstractions.CommonOptions.WriteBatch
member.summary: Accumulates multiple database write operations (inserts, updates, and tombstones) to be applied as a single, atomic unit.

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: Using a is the standard pattern for high-throughput transactional writes in LSM-tree engines. Grouping multiple operations into a single batch reduces disk synchronization overhead (fsync) when writing to the Write-Ahead Log (WAL), minimizes lock contention on the active MemTable, and ensures that either all operations succeed or none are committed (atomicity).

Performance Implications: Since this class allocates heap arrays (.ToArray()) to copy key-value spans into memory, excessively large batches can trigger high GC pressure or transient memory spikes. It is recommended to pool and reuse or size batches appropriately (e.g., in chunked increments) to balance latency and memory allocations.

member.name: T:Kdouja.Abstractions.CommonOptions.WriteOptions
member.summary: Configuration options governing behavior, durability guarantees, and lifespans of individual write operations in the storage engine.

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: Dictates how a transaction is processed down the write pipeline, determining whether it appends to the Write-Ahead Log (WAL) and whether it triggers synchronous disk flushes to maintain strict ACID persistence properties.

Performance Implications: Bypassing the WAL or disabling sync options yields massive write throughput boosts by avoiding disk I/O barriers, but reduces safety, exposing data to loss or corruption if the node unexpectedly crashes.

member.name: P:Kdouja.Abstractions.CommonOptions.WriteOptions.Sync
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the write operation blocks until the transaction is physically flushed to non-volatile disk storage (fsync).

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: If set to , the engine invokes a synchronous flush on the Write-Ahead Log (WAL) before acknowledging completion to the caller. If set to , data is written to operating system buffers and flushed asynchronously, which may result in data loss if a system crash or power outage occurs before the OS flushes buffers.

Performance Implications: Enabling synchronization severely reduces write throughput due to storage device write latency. Grouping multiple writes using or enabling group-commit mechanisms is recommended when sync is enabled.

member.name: P:Kdouja.Abstractions.CommonOptions.WriteOptions.DisableWal

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: When set to , the written records are stored directly into the volatile MemTable without appending them to the WAL. If the database crashes before the MemTable is flushed to an SSTable on disk, all data written with this flag set will be lost.
Performance Implications: Disabling the WAL is ideal for bulk loading scenarios or caching transient data where maximum ingestion rate is critical and data durability can be sacrificed.

member.name: T:Kdouja.Abstractions.Persistence.ISnapshot
member.summary: Represents an immutable, transactionally consistent read-only snapshot view of the database state at a specific sequence number.

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: Snapshots implement point-in-time isolation levels. When querying the database using an , any record committed with a sequence number higher than the snapshot's will be filtered out and invisible to the reader.

Performance Implications: Snapshots are extremely lightweight to create (simply capturing the current sequence number and incrementing a snapshot reference count). However, active snapshots defer garbage collection of old key versions (preventing compactions from purging overwritten/deleted keys), which can temporarily increase space amplification. It is critical to dispose of snapshots promptly.

member.name: T:Kdouja.Abstractions.Persistence.LevelMetadata
member.summary: Represents the metadata state, file collections, and size tracking for a single level (e.g., L0, L1, L2, etc.) within the LSM-tree.

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: The LSM-tree partitions data into levels. Level 0 (L0) is special because its SSTables can contain overlapping key ranges, requiring read lookups to check multiple tables. Higher levels (L1 and below) guarantee non-overlapping key ranges, allowing a read lookup to query at most one SSTable per level. Background compaction threads monitor level sizes and tables to trigger merge operations when limits are reached.

Concurrency: Instances of this class represent version state and are generally protected by immutable Version objects. When the file layout changes, a new version is created rather than modifying active instances in place, supporting lock-free MVCC reads.

member.summary: Defines the contract for managing cryptographic encryption keys and active key versions utilized by the secure page storage engine.

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: Enforces secure cryptographic key rotation and metadata mapping. Since the PageStore encrypts page data blocks before writing them to physical disk pages, this provider tracks which version of the key was used for encryption, enabling seamless decryption of historical pages even after a key rotation event has occurred.

Concurrency & Lifecycle: Implementations must guarantee thread-safe key access and lock-free lookup pathways on the read hot-path, preventing encryption key management from blocking concurrent I/O readers.

member.name: T:Kdouja.Abstractions.StoragePrimitives.IPageStore
member.summary: Defines the raw page-level physical I/O interface responsible for managing and accessing fixed-size block pages on disk.

remarks.para: Storage Engine Relevance: Acts as the block device abstraction layer directly above the operating system file system or hardware controller. The page size typically matches the physical hardware sector size (4096 bytes) to maximize transaction throughput when using Direct I/O. SSTables, manifests, and indexes are divided and stored across pages managed by this store.

Performance Implications: Operates on the critical path of both read and write operations. When is true, read/write operations bypass the OS page cache completely. As a result, the memory buffers passed to this store must align to physical page boundaries to avoid alignment faults.
